leads.location: Sitka, with operations in Juneau and Ketchikan
leads.why_picked: Highest fit total across all four scout segments. The operational pain is published in their own live job posting, the contact is verifiable on their own domain, and they publicly recommitted to day tours after closing their overnight line for overhead reasons.
leads.contact_source: https://allenmarinetours.com/contact-us/ (general Sitka office inbox, verified live three times, no personal address is published anywhere)
leads.outcome: Reduce the cost and recovery time of a changed sailing day, and make that cost visible for the first time.
leads.recommended_build: Sailing Day Control, v1 downscoped to the Operating Day Ledger. One port, read-only shared state, structured change capture, templated fan out, acknowledgement tracking, immutable event log. ZERO AI in v1.
leads.roi_summary: Two to three week instrumentation slice priced as decision data. Conservative recovers 105 percent of cost at month 12 (break even), most likely 196 percent at month 6, aggressive 345 percent at month 4. Payback four to twelve months. Both cash lines are spend avoided with us, conditional on a winter build being on their table.
leads.draft_subject: Allen Marine field study, free, and the build we recommend has no AI in it
leads.sent_note: Sent by Talon by hand after review, with light edits to voice and the closing ask. The routine drafted only.

leads.segment: other labor-scarce or paperwork-heavy Alaska SMBs
leads.why_picked: Employee-owned environmental research and consulting firm. Won a four-way tie at fit_total 23 on the substance of the verified contact path, a named president and a public business email both on fetched pages at a firm small enough that she reads her own mail.
leads.contact_source: verified on two independent ABR pages, her own bio page and the Senior NEPA Specialist posting. Not pattern-derived.
leads.outcome: Study shipped, build NOT recommended at observable volume. The conservative ROI case does not clear and the study says so in its section heading. Break-even needs about 31 past-performance-bearing submissions a year. The ask is that ABR count their own submissions, with the line named below which nobody should build it including us. Two things handed over free, a drafted homepage paragraph and a post-season data validation rule list.
leads.recommended_build: A cited search and assembly tool over an audited corpus of ABR's own approved proposal text, deterministic search shipped first as the baseline any model layer must beat. Phase one contains NO model. It retrieves and cites, code assembles, a human writes, and it never touches a determination.
leads.roi_summary: Computed in scripts/roi_math.py, never narrated. Conservative $36,600 cost, $8,861 return, 24 percent recovered, no payback in five years. Most likely $29,820, $31,696, 106 percent, payback month 57. Aggressive $23,575, $91,661, 389 percent, payback month 19. Break-even 31.1 submissions a year. NO ROW MARKED VERIFIED, which is the honest state of a business nobody has measured.
leads.notes: study-critic took NINE rounds to ship. It caught a fabricated 96-to-99-percent statistic that does not exist in its cited paper, an unread buy-versus-build multiple, an architecture diagram whose renderer labelled our own work as the prospect's, and a demo broken by a one-word edit. Two machine fixes were committed, build_study_page.py and FIELD_STUDY_SPEC.md. Known deviation: the page runs about 4,470 words against the spec's 2,000 to 3,000 budget, a 49 percent overrun, adjudicated across review rounds and accepted.
